subject: EquinoxMed service disruption — rapid update / next steps
messages:
From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@equinoxmed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden spike in inference errors / potential PHI exposure?

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a spike in 500 errors and elevated latency on our production calls to the Redwood API around 08:40 PST this morning. Error rate rose from ~0.3% to ~6% and a subset of requests returned truncated responses. Our integration handles PHI (hashed tokens) — we're concerned about any potential leakage or misrouting.

I've attached a short log snippet showing the failing request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this is a regional incident on your side, and whether patient identifiers might have been logged or forwarded? We need an initial assessment within 30 minutes if possible.

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Sr. Engineering Manager, Integrations
EquinoxMed

Attachment: initial-incident-log-snippet.txt (text/plain)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@equinoxmed.com>, Daniel Park <dpark@equinoxmed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in inference errors / potential PHI exposure?

Ava — thanks for the heads up and the log snippet. We see this on our monitoring as a regionally-scoped degradation affecting west-us inference nodes.

Immediate actions we are taking (bridge at 09:25 PST):
- Stand up a joint bridge (link sent separately) and add your engineering lead.
- Fail open route for your production traffic to a dedicated pool (best-effort) while we investigate KV-cache and batching behavior.
- Engineering will snapshot relevant logs (we've started a retention hold) and hunt for any non-standard egress.

We do not have evidence yet of PHI leakage; we will confirm after log review. Marcus (CS lead), Laura (runtime), and Stephanie (support) are on the thread. Marcus — please coordinate the bridge invite and confirm the estimated impact window.

I will send an executive status note to the Equinox leadership in the next 30 minutes.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: (referenced)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Collins <ava.collins@equinoxmed.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Sudden spike in inference errors / potential PHI exposure? — internal action items

On Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 09:18 AM PST Neha Kapoor wrote:
> Ava — thanks for the heads up and the log snippet. We see this on our monitoring as a regionally-scoped degradation affecting west-us inference nodes.

Internal note / runbook steps (I started a PagerDuty incident: INC-3421):
- Laura: primary on-site for kernel/quant path analysis. Initial suspicion: a regression in continuous-batching kernel selection causing partial KV-cache invalidation and increased OOMs under your median sequence profile.
- Stephanie: please queue the dedicated pool failover now and confirm capacity; I opened a fast-track capacity request.
- Ops: set conservative batching for EquinoxMed to 1–2 requests per batch until further notice.
- Compliance: archive all involved request/response payloads in the secure evidence bucket (read-only) for retention and audit.

I've attached the kv-cache dump for 08:35–09:05 PST for Laura's review. Will update with bridge link and ETA once we confirm the mitigation path.

Marcus Lin
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-cache-logs-20260108.tar.gz

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@equinoxmed.com>, Daniel Park <dpark@equinoxmed.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: EquinoxMed — executive summary (initial) | 09:44 PST

Ava / Daniel —

Thank you again for flagging this. Below is an initial executive summary for your leadership and compliance teams; more detail will follow after log review.

What happened (initial):
- Start: ~08:40 PST, Jan 8, 2026.
- Impact: Elevated 500 error rate (peak ~6%) and increased token latency for a subset of requests from west-us. Scope appears limited to calls routed to a specific runtime variant.

What we're doing now:
- Live bridge established (09:25 PST) including Redwood runtime and CS leads.
- Mitigation: Failover to reserved/dedicated pool for EquinoxMed traffic completed at 09:30 PST (best-effort); we reduced batching to conservative levels.
- Investigation: Engine team is analyzing KV-cache behavior and kernel selection; logs have been snapshot and secured.
- Data safety: No evidence to date of PHI exfiltration; all artifacts are under forensics hold. We'll confirm once the audit completes.

Next updates:
- 10:15 PST — technical findings from runtime lead (Laura).
- 13:00 PST — preliminary incident impact summary and proposed remediation steps.

Requested from EquinoxMed: please confirm if you want Redwood to perform a formal postmortem with redacted request payloads sent to your security team, and whether you prefer a phone briefing or written report.

We take this seriously and will share a full postmortem with timelines and corrective actions within 72 hours.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

--
Neha's signature: Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform.

Thanks Neha — that level of detail is helpful. We want the formal postmortem and a redacted payload bundle sent to our security team. Phone brief preferred (we can do 13:30 PST).

One request: please include in the postmortem whether the KV-cache invalidation could surface patient identifiers in logs that are not typically captured by our integration. Our compliance officer will need that clearly addressed.

Appreciate the rapid response.

—Ava
